question: For this read-only workload, which interconnect finishes sooner at equal 16 KiB capacity: an 8x8 full crossbar with 8 banks (A) or a radix-4 butterfly with 16 banks (B)?

implemented: Pinned RTL and toolchain, verified against locks
Verilator harness with 14 counted monitors and an independent event checker
Harness validation: 21/21 checks, every monitor catches an injected fault
L/B/M measured; strict reversal on M
Python and compiled C++ fast models, cross-checked event-for-event
Six-case discovery screen with six deterministic search methods
Unrestricted formal proof of 10 transport properties on the 2x2 harness
Structural repair accepted on two sealed held-out baskets; three wrong repairs rejected
Measured internal router activity from diagnostic traces
Static, Cloudflare-ready viewer over executed artifacts
Decision map: 289 workloads on both RTL designs; the bank-only model picks the wrong design in 11 and cannot decide in 16 more; the repaired model: 2 and 14
not_done: Model speed: 1.7x end-to-end (5x target not met; simulation kernel alone 2-8x). Process start-up and workload I/O dominate; Verilator is already fast on this small design.
No independently authored or naturally occurring audit case

global_limitations: Cycles at a common abstract clock; no silicon speed, area, power or frequency claim.
RTL simulation is a reference implementation, not fabricated silicon.
Audit cases were authored by the implementer; none is independently authored or naturally occurring.

properties.statement: at most one accepted initiator per bank per cycle
each bank acceptance carries an accepted initiator's row
RespLat=1: vld_o[i] at t+1 iff a read of initiator i was accepted at t
response data is routed from the accepted bank
no responses while reset is asserted
LIC work conservation: a requested, granting bank accepts someone
RIFT wrapper monitors never fire under the environment assumptions
a locked bank arbiter only holds requests that are still being made (strengthening invariant)

assumptions: reset asserted in the first cycle only, then deasserted permanently
no requests while reset is asserted
an unaccepted request keeps req_i and add_i stable in the next cycle
bank grants gnt_i and bank read data rdata_i are unconstrained (symbolic)

claims.all_properties_stall_le3_assumptions: listed assumptions plus: every bank stall lasts at most 3 consecutive cycles

assertion_exclusions.json.summary: Every concurrent vendor assertion in the elaborated closure is guarded by `ifndef VERILATOR and therefore did not execute in any RIFT simulation. Vendor elaboration-time initial assertions are compiled because Verilator ignores translate_off pragmas; they hold for all RIFT configurations and leave no residual runtime code. RIFT does not claim that vendor assertions executed and passed. RIFT's own boundary monitors are listed in docs/monitor_inventory.md and are counted per run.

items.name: initial assert(!(LockIn && ExtPrio))
items.note: THE LockIn/ExtPrio CONFLICT: xbar passes LockIn=1 unconditionally while bfly_net instantiates xbar with ExtPrio=1. With ExtPrio=1 rr_arb_tree takes the gen_ext_rr branch, so the LockIn branch is not elaborated. Under a non-Verilator frontend this assertion would reject the BFLY4 configuration. RIFT preserves the source unmodified and records the exclusion; any alternative simulator/formal frontend requires an explicit disposition before its results are accepted.

items.name: lock: LockIn |-> req_o && (!gnt_i && !flush_i) |=> idx_o == $past(idx_o)
items.note: inside gen_lock; elaborated only for LIC

items.name: lock_req: assume property (unserved requests not deasserted)
items.note: RIFT checks the equivalent driver obligation with monitor C1_REQUEST_STABILITY

assertion_exclusions.json.disposition: No vendor source was patched. No global assertion disable was used (--assert is on). RIFT's acceptance relies on its own counted monitors and independent event checking, not on vendor assertion counts.

defines.VERILATOR: implicitly defined by Verilator; selects the `ifndef VERILATOR exclusions recorded in locks/assertion_exclusions.json

preprocessing.json.translate_off_semantics: Verilator 5.053 does not honour `// pragma translate_off`; code inside those regions is compiled and executed (verified by tests/test_toolchain_semantics.py). Vendor elaboration-time initial assertions are therefore live and are constant-folded when they hold.
preprocessing.json.parameters_by_config: taken from configs/<config_id>.json and passed as -G overrides on rift_tcdm_top and -D defines for oracle/main.cpp
